name: Fox eye thread lift

lead: The fox eye look is an upward-slanting, elongated eye shape with a lifted outer corner and brow tail. The thread version uses absorbable threads, usually PDO, placed around the brow and temple to pull tissue up and outward in a clinic.

The term comes from social media and cosmetic clinic marketing, and on looksmaxxing forums where related options include tape and canthoplasty. Thread lifts in general suspend soft tissue by anchoring absorbable sutures under the skin; here the aim is raising the lateral brow and eye corner. A separate laser protocol called the fox eyes lift, using Er:YAG and Nd:YAG wavelengths, has been studied in a split-face study for eyebrow elevation. No published trial tests threads for this specific look.

paras: It is a short in-clinic procedure with threads placed around the brow and temple, and clinics report the lift is visible afterward. Some people compare it with taping at home or with surgical canthoplasty, which is a different and more invasive route to the same shape.

Reviews of thread lifts in general describe mostly minor, self-limiting events. The area around the eye has delicate tissue, and surgical fox eye procedures such as canthoplasty have drawn commentary, including a study that rated YouTube content on aesthetic canthoplasty as mostly poor quality and advertising-oriented. Threads are medical devices placed by clinicians.

web.title: Thread lift (Wikipedia; resolved to the Facelift article)

angle.text: Absorbable threads lift the outer brow, tilting the eye corner upward for a foxy, upturned eye shape. Clinics report the lift is visible after treatment; no published study tests threads for this specific look.

lead: 'Fox eyes' refers to an eye appearance with an upward-angled outer corner and lifted brow tail, popularised through social media and aesthetic clinics. A 'fox eye thread lift' is a minimally invasive procedure that uses absorbable threads, commonly polydioxanone, to lift the brow and lateral eye region toward that shape. [1]

No published clinical trial testing threads specifically for the fox-eye aesthetic was identified. Related literature includes a split-face study of a laser protocol called the 'fox eyes lift' for eyebrow elevation, a letter about fox eye surgery, and a study of the quality of online canthoplasty videos. [2][3]
Within looksmaxxing communities 'fox eyes' are discussed as an attractive eye shape, with talk of surgery, threads and home methods such as taping. [4]

paras: Thread lifts suspend soft tissue using sutures placed beneath the skin; reviews describe absorbable and barbed variants used in the midface, brow and neck.  Wikipedia describes barbed threads used without skin excision to lift face and neck skin. [1]
Wikipedia's canthoplasty entry describes canthoplasty as surgery on the medial or lateral canthus, used for cosmetic or functional reasons, and does not mention a fox-eye trend. [5]

No studies found on threads for fox eyes specifically. A prospective, interventional split-face study of 21 subjects (19 women, mean age 50) compared a new Fotona laser protocol called 'fox eyes lift' with a standard protocol for eyebrow elevation, using Er:YAG and Nd:YAG wavelengths over three monthly sessions. [2] This is a laser procedure, not a thread lift.
A study analysing 173 YouTube videos on aesthetic canthoplasty rated most as poor in quality and reliability, with a large share functioning as advertisements.

General thread-lift reviews report mostly minor and self-limiting adverse events and note that long-term efficacy data for absorbable threads are lacking.  Wikipedia reports a BBC investigation of thread-lift practitioners that found no mandatory qualifications in the UK. [1]
A letter in the Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery discusses fox eye surgery and the question of whom surgeons operate on. [3]

On looksmax.org, one thread asks whether sleeping with tape stretching the outer eyes can produce fox eyes; a reply says it would only loosen the skin, which is the poster's view. [4] No studies of eye taping for this purpose were identified.

lore.intro: Forum posts mention fox eyes alongside taping, surgery and bonesmashing, but community material is thin. [4]
